lesson.title: Now the Line Opens
lesson.hook: Two connected choices. Watch what your first shot creates.
lesson.liveIntro: This ball is shorter. You have time to set on the backhand, and they are recovering toward the crosscourt side.

to1A.name: What does their reply permit now?
to1A.sit: They stretch to the line and send a shorter reply toward the middle.
to1A.q: What does their reply permit now?
opts: Use controlled depth into the space
Lift through the middle to regain time

lines.A: You move forward and use the space with a generous target.
lines.B: A sound reset. You also had a shorter ball to work with.

to1A.take: The line changes with your contact. Read what makes it available.
to1A.payoff: The line changes with your contact. Read what makes it available.
to1A.principle: Use the opening you earn. Cover the reply it creates.
to1A.why: Compared with the stretched wide ball, this contact is closer, higher and better organised. The opponent is also away from the line. Controlled depth can use that opening; the next reply still needs a fresh read.

to1B.name: What does their reply permit now?
to1B.sit: They step into your short ball and send you back out to the backhand.
to1B.q: What does their reply permit now?
opts: Use controlled depth into the space
Lift through the middle to regain time

lines.A: The space is there, but the deeper contact makes pressing less comfortable.
lines.B: You adapt to the deeper ball and regain recovery time.

opts: Use controlled depth down the open line

lines.A: Your balanced contact lets you use the line with margin. Watch how they defend.
lines.B: The shorter float gives them time to step in. Read their deeper reply.

pro.label: Djokovic · Change what the rally allows
pro.moment: Djokovic’s 51 run-around forehands disrupted Ruud’s preferred backhand-court pattern in the 2022 Turin final. His backhand changes down the line then became part of a broader attack. The opening grew out of the exchange.
pro.read: Your next point: here you have time, balance and an opponent across the court. Use that opening—and compare it with the earlier rushed ball.
pro.src: ATP Brain Game · Djokovic–Ruud, Turin final 2022

drill.name: Two-ball read
drill.how: Alternate a deep wide backhand feed and a shorter one. Recover toward the crosscourt side as feeder. Let the receiver call the opening, then play your actual reply.
